sections.title: Every entry is a tile. Your apps are the mosaic.
sections.subtitle: Tess is a self-hostable headless CMS in a single Rust binary. Define your content models at runtime and get a typed GraphQL API instantly, on the database you already run. **And manage it all by talking to your AI assistant**, through the built-in MCP server.

sections.title: Manage your website by talking to your AI
sections.body:
Ask Claude, Cursor or any MCP client to write, edit and publish your content: Tess speaks the **Model Context Protocol** out of the box. Your assistant discovers your content models by itself, then reads and writes through the same API and permissions as your apps.

- **No plugin, no glue code:** turn it on with `TESS_MCP=true` and add one entry to your AI client.
- **Safe by default:** give the assistant a Contributor token and it can only write drafts, which your team reviews and publishes.
- **Works with every model** you create, the moment you create it.

[See how it works →](/ai)
sections.code:
You: Find every published post without a meta
     description and write one for each, as drafts.

AI:  Found 12 posts. I've drafted a description
     for each one and submitted them for review.

You: Add a "Summer sale" banner to the home page
     for next week, and show me the draft.

sections.title: Everything a content team needs, nothing to rebuild
sections.subtitle: Tess keeps the business rules in one place, so the GraphQL API, the admin UI, uploads and plugins all behave the same.

sections.title: A content model is one mutation away
sections.body:
Create a content type and Tess generates its queries, filters, sorting, pagination and mutations on the spot, on every instance.

Prefer clicking? The admin UI has a model editor. Prefer files? Keep your models in YAML and import them with `tess-transfer`.

sections.title: How does Tess compare?
sections.subtitle: Honest, dated comparisons with the CMSs you probably know, including when they are the better choice.

sections.title: Fun fact: Tess runs on a Raspberry Pi 3
sections.body:
Tess's creator runs their own Tess on a **Raspberry Pi 3**, without n8n: one Rust binary, an embedded database, and nothing else to install. It uses about 30 MB of memory while idle, so even a 1 GB board has plenty of room left.

- **No database server needed:** RocksDB or SQLite are built in.
- **Native ARM builds:** `arm64` and `armv7` binaries and `arm64` Docker images with every release.
- **Pi 4 and 5 too**, with room for n8n, PostgreSQL and search on the bigger boards.

[Run Tess on a Raspberry Pi →](/docs/devops/raspberry-pi)
sections.code:
# On the Pi (64-bit Raspberry Pi OS)
VERSION=0.1.1
curl -LO https://github.com/tessheadless/core/releases/download/v$VERSION/tess-$VERSION-linux-arm64.tar.xz
tar -xJf tess-$VERSION-linux-arm64.tar.xz
cd tess-$VERSION-linux-arm64

cp .env.example .env   # add your secrets
set -a && . ./.env && set +a && ./tess
# → http://raspberrypi.local:8080/admin/

items.question: Is Tess free?
items.answer: The **Community** edition is free for personal use. Commercial use needs the **Enterprise** edition, which also adds advanced features, official plugins and hosting. See [Community & Enterprise](/docs/editions).

items.question: Can AI tools manage my content?
items.answer: Yes. Tess has a built-in [MCP server](/ai): connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client with an API token, and ask it in plain language to create, edit, translate or publish content. It can do exactly what the token's role allows, nothing more.

items.question: Which database do I need?
items.answer: None to start: Tess embeds RocksDB. In production use PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB or DynamoDB, or keep SQLite or RocksDB for small sites.

items.question: Can Tess run on a Raspberry Pi?
items.answer: Yes. Tess's creator runs it on a Raspberry Pi 3. Every release has native `arm64` and `armv7` Linux binaries and `arm64` Docker images, for the Pi 3, 4 and 5. See [Raspberry Pi & small devices](/docs/devops/raspberry-pi).

items.question: Is there a REST API?
items.answer: Content is served over GraphQL only. REST endpoints exist for binary payloads: media uploads and downloads, plugin modules.

items.question: Can I move my models from another CMS?
items.answer: Describe them in the `tess-transfer` YAML format and import them in one command. Each [comparison page](/compare) explains how a model maps to Tess.

sections.title: Run Tess in one command
sections.body: `docker compose up`, open the admin, create your first model.

features.title: Run it with AI
features.summary: A built-in MCP server lets Claude, Cursor and any MCP client read your models and create, edit and publish content in plain language, with the same permissions as the API.

features.title: Models at runtime
features.summary: Create content types in the admin or through the API, in production. The GraphQL schema is regenerated on the fly: no rebuild, no redeploy.

features.title: GraphQL-first
features.summary: Typed queries, filters, sorting, pagination, relations and mutations generated for every model, with a GraphiQL IDE built in.

features.title: Your database
features.summary: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, DynamoDB or embedded RocksDB. Every backend passes the same conformance suite.

features.title: Review workflows
features.summary: Draft and publish for every entry, plus an optional submit → approve workflow per content type, in every edition.

features.title: Roles and scoped tokens
features.summary: Owner, Admin, Contributor, Reviewer and Member roles, limited to some content types if needed, and scoped API tokens for machines.

features.title: Sandboxed plugins
features.summary: WebAssembly plugins installed by admins at runtime, written in Rust, Go, JavaScript and more, with timeouts and memory limits.

features.title: Serverless or container
features.summary: One binary runs as an HTTP server (Docker, VM, Kubernetes) or as an AWS Lambda function.

features.title: Media library
features.summary: Uploads to S3-compatible stores (Garage, MinIO, AWS S3, Cloudflare R2) or the local filesystem, with direct presigned uploads.

features.title: Full-text search
features.summary: Typesense indexing kept in sync with your content, behind a pluggable search engine interface.

features.title: Private by design
features.summary: Opaque, expiring, encrypted ids in the API: database ids never leave the server.

features.title: Portable models
features.summary: tess-transfer exports content models and users to YAML or JSON, to version them or copy them between instances.

competitors.name: Strapi
competitors.summary: The most popular open-source headless CMS, built on Node.js, with a REST API and a GraphQL plugin.

competitors.name: Hygraph
competitors.summary: A hosted, GraphQL-native CMS (formerly GraphCMS), known for content federation across remote APIs.

competitors.name: WordPress
competitors.summary: The world's most used CMS, a PHP application with themes, plugins and a REST API, often used headless through WPGraphQL.

competitors.name: Contentful
competitors.summary: An enterprise headless CMS delivered as SaaS, with REST and GraphQL delivery APIs and a large app ecosystem.

competitors.name: Directus
competitors.summary: A Node.js platform that turns an existing SQL database into REST and GraphQL APIs with an admin app.

competitors.name: Payload
competitors.summary: An open-source TypeScript CMS configured in code, which installs inside a Next.js application.

competitors.name: Sanity
competitors.kind: Hosted content platform with an open-source studio
competitors.summary: A hosted Content Lake with a customizable, open-source React editing studio and its own query language, GROQ.
